newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Boland Bank takes up option in Monex.
newsitem.headline: Boland Bank takes up option in Monex.

text.p: South Africa's Boland Bank has exercised its option to buy a significant stake in property developer Monex, Boland managing director Michiel le Roux said on Wednesday.
"We believe Century City, the major development being undertaken by Monex (outside Cape Town), is an excellent project," Le Roux said in a statement.
"The management of Monex has succeeded in substantially reducing the company's debt, which dates from the time when it was known as Ilco Homes, and placing it on a firm business footing again."

When the management of Monex Development Company started straightening out the affairs of heavily indebted Ilco in 1995, it acquired 86 percent of Ilco's issued share capital as one of the conditions of the rescue package.
Ilco and its holding cmpany owed Boland Bank 83 million rand at that stage.

At the same time, Boland Bank negotiated an option to take up 50 percent of the management's shareholding. "I believe that exercising this option will in the long term be of considerable benefit to Boland Bank shareholders," Le Roux said.

As the transaction involves a change in control, Boland Bank will have to make a standby offer to minority shareholders. The Securities Regulation Panel has stipulated that this offer should be 57 cents a share.
